publication.retry_plan_error: HTTP 503 integration_unavailable: Review scopes must be distinct; only the validator gate has no scopes

diagnosis.classification: Upstream IAM/Honeycomb review-plan provider-name collision after canonical application identifiers; not an ordinary missing external-scope approval.

live_configuration_evidence.source: Authenticated canonical Honeycomb apps get for ting and honeycomb; no secrets retained.

source_evidence.finding: IAM groups critical external scopes by catalog.app_id, yielding provider honeycomb for this scope, then appends a separate empty validator gate also named honeycomb.
Honeycomb requires unique provider names and reserves honeycomb for the empty validator gate. Its nonempty-scopes rejection exactly matches the observed HTTP 503.

IAM returns the stored immutable plan for an existing request. Preapproving the external scope alone does not resolve the duplicate provider: the gate filter retains every provider named honeycomb even after scopes are removed.

diagnosis.release_side_remedy: None that preserves the existing required Honeycomb scope and normal review policy. Do not remove or rename Ting scopes, edit stored plans, or bypass provider/validator review.
diagnosis.supported_next_action: Fix the upstream IAM/Honeycomb contract to distinguish the validator gate from the Honeycomb application provider. Then use the supported configuration/publication workflow to generate a fresh immutable plan for a new revision and complete all required provider and validator approvals. Retrying the existing request alone replays its stored malformed plan.

limitations: Production IAM endpoint registration is verified; end-to-end read-state acceptance is verified separately.
Public Honeycomb publication remains blocked by review-plan validation; no approval bypass was attempted.
